summary: The 1935 Oswald Dome fire tower was taken down in 2003; a segment with its cab now stands as an exhibit at the Ocoee Whitewater Center.

facts.status_note: The tower is no longer on Oswald Dome. A segment with its cab is an exhibit at the Ocoee Whitewater Center.

access.note: Reached by Oswald Dome Road, a Forest Service road off U.S. 64, and by two trails. Communication towers and transmitters now stand on the summit.

visit.trail_note: The Oswald Dome Trail climbs about 2,200 feet in just under four miles from Quinn Springs Recreation Area. A pickup or SUV is recommended for the dirt road.

events.note: Built on Bean Mountain, also called Oswald Dome. The marker gives 79 ft 6 in; Tennessee Landforms says 80 ft.
Disassembled and removed from its original location, per the marker.
A segment with its cab was restored and set up at the Ocoee Whitewater Center.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The marker gives 79 ft 6 in; Tennessee Landforms says an 80-foot tower. The story and facts use the marker's figure.

Wikipedia says a fire tower was moved in 2004; the marker says only a segment of the tower structure with its cab was relocated, and Tennessee Landforms says only the top or cab section. The story follows the marker.
Not a real conflict: the marker dates the removal from the mountain to 2003 and the setup at the Ocoee Whitewater Center to 2004.

notes_for_editor: Fate and the 1935 build rest mostly on one historical marker erected by Cherokee National Forest. Wikipedia's 'a fire tower was moved' is looser than the marker and Tennessee Landforms, which describe only a segment with its cab; the story follows the marker. facts.height_m uses the marker's overall 79 ft 6 in; the marker does not say whether that is to the cab floor. Record elevation 922.9 m (Tennessee Landforms, 3028 ft) differs from Wikipedia's 3,022 ft; not changed. 'Bean Mountain' is a second name Wikipedia gives and could be added to other_names; Eastern US Lookouts lists 'Oswald Bald' with no history. Facebook posts (Visit Ocoee and Discover McCaysville) repeat 1935 and 2004 but could not be fetched (login wall), so they are not cited. Wikipedia's Ocoee Whitewater Center page notes that its visitor center burned in April 2022; no source here says whether the exhibit was affected. The exhibit has its own record (us-tn-ocoee). Page reads exceeded the six-per-tower budget.
